options.label: Graphics backend
options.description: How melonDS draws the DS's 3D. OpenGL can draw at a higher resolution; Software is the most accurate. 'Software, OpenGL display' keeps the Software 3D but shows the picture through OpenGL, which the screen filter and VSync need.

options.label: Internal resolution
options.description: Draws the 3D at a multiple of the DS's 256x192 for a sharper picture. Only the OpenGL backends use it. Higher costs speed.

options.label: Aspect ratio
options.description: The shape of each DS screen. 4:3 is the DS's own; the wider ones stretch the picture.

options.label: Integer scaling
options.description: Scales the screens by whole numbers only, so every DS pixel has the same size. Leaves borders.

options.label: Screen filter
options.description: How the picture is scaled up to the screen. Sharp keeps edges crisp; Smooth blends them. Needs an OpenGL backend or the OpenGL display.

options.label: VSync
options.description: Waits for the screen's refresh to stop tearing. Can add a little input lag. Needs an OpenGL backend or the OpenGL display.

notes: Verified against melonDS-emu/melonDS tag 1.1 (b86390e), src/frontend/qt_sdl, the source pkgforge-dev/melonDS-AppImage 1.1-2 packages. Config is ~/.config/melonDS/melonDS.toml (Config.cpp:40), parsed with toml11 4.2.0 (toml/toml11/version.hpp). Every setting is read through a dotted path ('3D.GL.ScaleFactor'), each part a nested table (Config.cpp:648-661 ResolvePath), so the sections here are the TOML table headers melonDS itself writes: [3D], [3D.GL], [Screen], [Instance0.Window0]. Values are TOML literals: integers, and booleans true/false (Table::GetInt/GetBool fall back to the default when the type is wrong, Config.cpp:556-590).

melonDS rewrites the WHOLE file on ROM load (Window.cpp:1463 updateRecentFilesMenu -> Config::Save), when a window closes (Window.cpp:849) and at exit (main.cpp:400; OpenGamepadUI's SIGTERM ends it before that), from its in-memory table: toml11 writes `key = value`, tables as [a.b] headers with a blank line after each table body (toml/toml11/serializer.hpp:901-963), every key melonDS has read included. A TOML syntax error leaves the table empty (Config.cpp:796-803) and the next save empties the file: emuopts validates every patched file with tomllib first.

HAZARD (melonDS never run yet): a file with [3D.GL] but no [3D] header makes [3D] an IMPLICIT table in toml11 (toml/toml11/parser.hpp:2196-2207); melonDS then adds 3D.Renderer to it on start, and Config::Save throws 'an implicit table cannot have non-table value' (serializer.hpp:700-716) AFTER opening the file with trunc (Config.cpp:809-819): melonDS aborts and melonDS.toml is left empty. Both seeds therefore carry [3D] Renderer = 0 (melonDS's default), so a resolution chosen before melonDS's first run lands under an explicit [3D]. Once melonDS has saved, [3D] is always there (it reads 3D.Renderer at every start, Window.cpp:864-865).

renderer: [3D] Renderer int, 0 Software, 1 OpenGL, 2 OpenGL compute (EmuInstance.h:70-78; range clamp Config.cpp:80; default Software Config.cpp:56; Video settings radio buttons VideoSettingsDialog.cpp:70-73). Read when the emulator thread starts (EmuThread.cpp:122-127). [Screen] UseGL bool (no default: false) is melonDS's 'Use OpenGL display' checkbox, only meaningful with Software (VideoSettingsDialog.cpp:41-45); OpenGL is used when UseGL or a GL renderer (EmuInstance.cpp:370-374, Window.cpp:864-865). Every choice writes both so the Software choices can say which display they use; true for the GL backends matches what they do anyway. If the GL context cannot be created melonDS falls back to Software and SAVES Renderer 0 / UseGL false (Window.cpp:877-884); the emulator-level choice is written again at the next launch. melonDS has no Vulkan backend.

resolution: [3D.GL] ScaleFactor int 1..16 (default 1 Config.cpp:57, clamp Config.cpp:82; the dialog lists 1..16 as 'Nx native (256N x 192N)', VideoSettingsDialog.cpp:96-98). Used by the OpenGL and compute renderers only, when the renderer is set up (EmuThread.cpp:894-902); the dialog disables it for Software (VideoSettingsDialog.cpp:46). RetroForge offers up to 5x (user, 2026-10-16: 5x already fills a 1080p panel); higher steps stay in the emulator's own menu.

aspect: [Instance0.Window0] ScreenAspectTop and ScreenAspectBot ints, the aspectRatios ids 0 4:3 (native), 4 5:3 (3DS), 1 16:9, 2 21:9, 3 window (fill the screen's area) (Screen.h:41-50; clamp Config.cpp:90-91; default 0). Both are written with the same value, read when the window's screen panel loads its config (Screen.cpp:120-132). There is no 'auto': the DS is always 4:3.
integer_scale: [Instance0.Window0] IntegerScaling bool (default false; Screen.cpp:129, menu Window.cpp:564-566, 2138-2142).

smoothing: [Instance0.Window0] ScreenFilter bool, GL_LINEAR when true, GL_NEAREST when false (Screen.cpp:88, 1153-1155; Window.cpp:2150-2155). The menu item is disabled without OpenGL (Window.cpp:905) and the Qt (non-GL) panel always draws nearest. The 'Screen.Filter' default (Config.cpp:98) and legacy mapping (Config.cpp:209) are dead: nothing reads that path, so the window key defaults to false (sharp).

vsync: [Screen] VSync bool (no default: false), applied with VSyncInterval when the OpenGL context is set up (EmuInstance.cpp:390-397); no effect without OpenGL (VideoSettingsDialog.cpp:147-151). VSyncInterval is left alone (1..20, default 1, Config.cpp:55, 81).

Window keys are those of Instance0.Window0 only. On a dual-screen board that is the top screen's window; the bottom screen's window (Instance0.Window1, its own table in melonDS-dual-screen.toml, Window.cpp:234 copies Window0 only when Window1 is empty) keeps melonDS's defaults, and is not touched here with the layout keys (ScreenLayout, ScreenSizing, ScreenSwap, ScreenGap, ScreenRotation, Window1) that the launcher's seed choice owns.
Left out: widescreen_hack (melonDS has none), show_fps (melonDS shows the frame rate only in the window title, EmuThread.cpp:425-430, hidden in fullscreen; 'ShowOSD' is the message overlay, not FPS).
